plate.narration: A dragonling grandmother rings her bell at a prospector on her doorstep. Above the crowded tents, a black tower rises from the ridge. The road has brought everyone this far. Now there are questions to carry uphill.

objectives.label: Read the glassback crab's warning before anybody got pinched
Found the cold cinder wolves something to eat
Listened to the soup-tent woman all the way through

goal.text: Climb to the tower on the ridge, learn what the stones are, and say what it is all for.

steps.label: Learn what the stones really are
Say what it is all for

facet_table.name: The Table Stone
facet_table.text: From the Redspire truth-table. Logged twice. Hums whenever someone tells the truth.

scene_arrival.narration: Tonight's job: climb to the tower on the ridge, learn what the stones are, and say what it is all for. The foothills smell of warm rocks and burnt toast. On the ridge stands a black tower called Redspire Citadel, home of the Skywardens. Below it, a grandmother rings a bell at a man digging up her doorstep.

scene_door_river.narration: The warden engineers from the broken bridge walk down with you, still arguing about a crack. Behind you lie the pride roads and the river toll. Ahead is the tower, where their records can meet yours.

scene_door_wild.narration: The MossHome high paths end at a mossy step into ash. The moss stops at a ruler-straight line. A runner from the forest waves goodbye, and politely refuses to cross it.

scene_door_rush.narration: You climb up from the boundary stones among the rush wagons. Dragonling grandmothers ring a bell for every pick that passes. One has switched to a smaller bell to save her arm.

scene_doorstep.narration: A prospector named Dunmore has planted his claim flag on the grandmother's doorstep. "It hums!" he says. So does every stone up here. She rings louder. He goes pink, but keeps his pick. Her house has a round window with curtains.

choices.label: Stand on the step with her

check_doorstep.prompt: Stand firm on the grandmother's doorstep so Dunmore cannot dig

onSuccess.narration: You climb onto the step beside the grandmother and plant your feet. Nobody can dig up a doorstep with people standing on it. Dunmore looks at your boots, then at the little round window with curtains in it, and goes pinker than ever. "Sorry," he mumbles, and pulls up his flag. The grandmother gives him a cookie. He is so surprised that he says thank you twice.

onFailure.narration: You climb onto the step, and Dunmore's pick nudges your boots right off it again. Then the grandmother starts ringing her bell right beside his ear. In the end he gives up on the step just to get away from the noise, and stomps off up the slope, rubbing his ear and grumbling about bells.

scene_doorstep_dig_elsewhere.narration: You find Dunmore a humming boulder with no door in it. He plants his flag, very proud. The grandmother rings a sweet thank-you. Dunmore keeps waving long after you stop.

scene_doorstep_one_rule.narration: Your dragonling stands on the step and says the rule every dragonling door knows: "Take what the mountain drops. Never pry at what it holds." Dunmore takes off his hat. "Nobody told me," he says quietly, and writes it inside his hat.

scene_moths.narration: Embermoths huddle on the cold side of a rock, away from the warm cracks they love. One refuses to leave a prospector's soup. "I give up," he says, and eats around it.

choices.label: Say it: this is a warning
Count the moths. All of them.

scene_moths_follow.narration: The moths make an arrow down the slope, all facing away from the mountain. Something glows in the wagon ruts at its point.

scene_moths_coax.narration: You carry the soup moth to a warm crack. It walks straight back out, as if you offered it an oven. The prospector thanks you for his soup.

scene_moths_count.narration: Your bigfoot counts them. All of them. Three hundred and twelve embermoths, and every one faces away from the mountain, like an audience with its back to the stage.

scene_moths_say_it.narration: "Moths leaving the warm is a warning," says your dragonling, in a grandmother voice. A grandmother three tents away hears it and rings her hand bell once, sharp, toward the next town.

scene_wolves.narration: Cinder wolves lie heaped in the road like coals with ears, too cold and hungry to care about the wagons. "Off the road, you silly coals!" shouts a centaur drover. Every drover is shouting. Nobody is moving.

scene_wolves_wait.narration: At last the wolves stretch and wander off together. Every drover says their shouting did it. The road begins to move.

scene_wolves_fly_look.narration: From the air you spot a sausage cart tipped in the ditch, a hundred paces down. You fly a slow line toward it. The biggest wolf lifts its nose, and the whole pack flows after you like water down a drain.

check_wolves.prompt: Find the hungry wolves something better than the road

onSuccess.narration: You spot an overturned sausage cart in the ditch. The wolves spot it two seconds after you. The road clears in a hurry, and one wolf looks back at you as if it is memorizing your face.

onFailure.narration: Your plan involves a sausage on a string, and the wolves are not impressed. In the end they wander off on their own, howling long complaints at the mountain.

scene_claim_boulder.narration: Up the road, two prospectors stand on one humming boulder, each with a flag. "Mine," says the burrowfolk. "Mine," says the faun. They have tied their bootlaces to their flags. The crowd has brought snacks.

check_claim.prompt: Find out whose claim flag went into the boulder first

onSuccess.narration: You check the flag holes. Both are brand new. But under the moss at the bottom of the boulder is a third mark, a little carved line, so old the moss has grown into it. It was here before either of them. It was here before anyone. Both prospectors stare at it, untie their bootlaces, and go and find a different boulder, quietly.

onFailure.narration: You measure the flags, count the footprints, and ask the crowd. Everybody gives a different answer, and two people give three. In the end the boulder settles it by humming so loudly that both prospectors hop off at once, and neither of them wants to get back on.

scene_claim_boulder_share.narration: They chalk the round boulder in half, then argue about which half has the hum. At least they are sitting down now. The crowd claps.

scene_claim_boulder_show.narration: Your kitsune turns the argument into a play, with voices. The crowd laughs, cheers, then votes. The winner gets the boulder. The loser gets everybody's snacks. By the end, the winner wants to swap.

scene_claim_boulder_nobodys.narration: You hold up the Unassigned Stone and tell them about the grandmothers' old list of caves that belong to nobody. "Nobody's," says one prospector, trying the word. "Nobody's," says the other. They go and share a sandwich instead.

scene_soup_tent.narration: At the top of the road, a soup tent says FREE, NO QUESTIONS. A woman called Hessa Wren ladles soup for {party} and remembers every name. Helpers in painted bark masks stir the pots, humming one low note. "My friends from the Deep Hollow," she says. Then, kindly: "There's a seal on the mountain, like a lid on a pot. It's a cage on the cure. Will you help us open it?"

scene_soup_tent_ford_soup.narration: "You met Wend!" Hessa's face lights up. "Wend sends love to everybody, but Wend did say your names." She adds an extra spoonful to each bowl. It is the same soup. Somehow it tastes like the whole road north.

scene_soup_tent_mask.narration: Your kitsune nods at the bark mask in Hessa's apron pocket. She does not hide it. "For singing. The mountain likes a choir." She hums three notes, and the stones of the hillside hum back. She smiles like a gardener at a seedling.

scene_soup_tent_just_soup.narration: You just eat the soup. It is excellent, with barley and something green. Hessa watches kindly and patiently. When you hand back the bowls, she says, "Tomorrow, then," as if you had an appointment.

scene_soup_tent_no_thanks.narration: "No, thank you," you say. Hessa does not argue, does not stop smiling, and does not take the bowl back. "The soup isn't the pitch," she says. "The soup is just soup." You believe her about the soup.

scene_soup_tent_ask_cure.narration: Hessa thinks about it properly. "Who gets to be hungry," she says at last. "Who gets to be cold. Why the sky is the wrong color, and nobody with a ledger can say why." She refills your bowl. "Little things. Everything."

rest_warm_stones.narration: Dragonling neighbors offer you warm stones to sleep on. Their bell-keeper, Grandmother Tull, rings the night bell. A spare bell sits beside it, never rung. "That one is nothing to worry about," she says, and then says it again.

scene_morning_bells.narration: In the morning, Grandmother Tull teaches tiny dragonlings the bell calls on a bench. The spare bell is wrapped in a sock. "Nothing to worry about," says Tull. Up the ridge, the citadel watch is listening.

check_bells.prompt: Ring the morning ring in time with the little dragonlings

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding-ding, ding. You get it right, and the smallest dragonling gives you a solemn nod, as if you had joined something important. Grandmother Tull presses a warm honeycake into your hands for the climb, and tells you the ridge is that way, as if you might have forgotten.

onFailure.narration: Your ring comes out ding, dong, clatter, which in bell code means, as far as anyone can tell, goats, but sideways. The little dragonlings laugh so hard that one falls off the bench. Grandmother Tull says you will get it next time, and points you up the ridge.

scene_morning_bells_sock.narration: Grandmother Tull takes a long breath. "That one has never been rung. Everybody knows what it would mean, and nobody says it." She pats the sock like a sleeping dog. "Nothing to worry about." That is four times now. She does not quite look at you.

scene_morning_bells_fly_ring.narration: You fly a little bell up the ridge and ring it, one, two-two, one. Far below, tiny bells ring back, proud and not quite together. From up here you can see a crowd halfway up, around something that glitters.

scene_crab.narration: On the ridge, Dunmore raises his pick at a glittering heap. "It hums!" The heap has eyes and claws. It is a glassback crab, rocking on its warm ground. Another watches from the next burrow. Dunmore should really check for curtains first.

choices.label: Back off, go the long way

scene_crab_dunmore.narration: "Dunmore! Three big steps back!" He knows your voice now. He stops mid-swing and steps back, and the whole crowd steps back with him. The crab lowers its claws and goes back to tidying its pebbles.

check_crab.prompt: Read the glassback crab's threat display

onSuccess.narration: Two claws up and a rock to the left means: this is my warm ground, and you are standing in my garden. You tell everybody to take three big steps back. The crab lowers its claws and goes back to tidying its pebbles, very pleased.

onFailure.narration: Two claws up and a rock to the left means... you guess "hello." It does not mean hello. The crab charges, and its neighbor from the next burrow scuttles over to see what all the fuss is.

encounter_crab.narration: Two glassback crabs clatter down the switchbacks, shells flashing every color.

onVictory.narration: Both crabs back onto their warm ground and forget you ever existed. But it took all morning. The sun is high when you reach the citadel road.

onDefeat.narration: The crabs nudge you, very firmly, all the way down the ridge. You are fine. You are also at the bottom again, and the afternoon is nearly gone.

check_late_gate.prompt: Race the sunset up the ridge before the citadel gate closes

onSuccess.narration: You run the switchbacks two at a time and slide in under the gate as it comes down, with one finger's width to spare.

onFailure.narration: The gate comes down with a BOOM just as you get there. A warden on the wall gives you a sad little shrug. Rules are rules, even for heroes.

scene_crab_thanks.narration: Dunmore lowers his pick. The crab arranges three pebbles like a thank-you note. You could go straight up to the citadel now, or spend the morning helping the crowd find a safer spot.

scene_crab_thanks_help_dunmore.narration: You spend the morning finding the crowd a patch with no crab under it. By the last tent, the sun is high.

scene_crab_thanks_fly_ahead.narration: You fly ahead and land on the citadel wall, which is not allowed. The warden on the gate sighs. By the time the others arrive, the gate is open and a clerk is waiting with two ledgers.

scene_citadel_gate.narration: Every window in Redspire Citadel faces up. Inside, a warden clerk called Pellam writes your names in his ledger, then writes them again. "The captain has a table," he says.

scene_citadel_gate_windows.narration: "So we see it first," says Pellam. "Whatever the mountain does, a warden writes it down. Most nights the log says nothing." He looks proud. "Nothing is the best thing a log can say."

scene_citadel_gate_desk.narration: A sign says ANYTHING THAT HUMS, LOG IT HERE. Pellam dips his pen and waits, like a cat at a mouse hole. "I can log your packs," he says, "or explain the records."

scene_citadel_gate_desk_tip_out.narration: Pellam logs everything you show him, draws tiny pictures, and hands it all back. Then he stamps your hands LOGGED. "Honest on paper," he says. "The best kind." The ink will last for days.

scene_citadel_gate_desk_ask_why.narration: Pellam turns the big log around. Page after page of stones, four hundred years of them, each written down twice. "Every one of them went somewhere," he says. "Nobody ever wrote down where." The newest page is full. So is the one before.

scene_citadel_gate_desk_clerks.narration: Pellam reads the tag on the Clerk's Stone. It is in his own handwriting. "Logged at the bridge," he breathes. "Carried up. Here." He has to sit down. He writes HOME beside the stone and waves you on.

scene_pellam_again.narration: Pellam does not look up. "The bridge is logged. I go where the ledgers are." He writes your names a third time, in a tiny notebook for people he has met twice. "Irregular. Entirely legal. This way."

scene_truth_table.narration: At a long table of watch-logs and one humming stone waits Captain Orla Voss, who commands the Skywardens. "Show us what the road taught you," she says. "Then we'll show you what the logs say."

scene_truth_table_puzzle.prompt: Put the foothills together before the wardens read their logs

onSuccess.narration: You lay the last two days on the table: moths facing away, wolves too cold to hunt, a crab guarding its warm ground, a whole hillside of stones humming one note. "Everything up here is leaning away from the mountain," you say. Captain Voss pushes the oldest log across the table. "So did we," she says. "Four hundred years ago."

onFailure.narration: You lay out the moths, the wolves and the crab, and they go around and around and will not join up. Pellam clears his throat, very kindly, and opens the oldest log. "It took us four hundred years," he says. "You have had two days."

scene_truth_table_odd_ledger.narration: Your bigfoot points at one ledger in a different color, half hidden. Pellam looks caught stealing cookies. "That one's not read. It's only kept." Captain Voss holds out her hand. The room goes very quiet.

scene_truth_table_rush_clues.narration: You show the relay's spiral verses and the boundary tallies. They bend around the same places as the old watch-log. Voss lays them side by side. Pellam checks the dates, twice.

scene_truth_table_wild_clues.narration: You describe the wounded glades, the MossHome path archive and the knot-cord. Pellam sets them beside the old watch-log. "The forest keeps records too," says Voss.

scene_truth_table_river_clues.narration: You show the sash-maps and the bridge survey. Pellam sets a four-hundred-year-old log beside them. Its faded question matches the troll's: WHERE DID YOU GET THAT, AND WHERE IS IT GOING?

scene_whole_truth.narration: Your clues and the wardens' logs click together like a puzzle. The gemstones are pieces of a seal. The seal holds a titan asleep under Mount Red Sky. And the rush is taking the seal apart, one pocket at a time. On the table, the gemstone hums. One very old line says an old stone gate, far away in a western marsh, hums the same note. Beside it, in three different handwritings: nobody knows why.

scene_whole_truth_leave_stone.narration: "Custody," says Voss. Pellam adds it to both entries. The stone keeps humming on the table.

scene_whole_truth_take_stone.narration: Pellam logs the Table Stone under WITH THEM, a third time, and slides it across. It hums in your palm while Voss unrolls her map.

scene_acceptable_losses.narration: Voss circles three towns on her map. "Acceptable losses," she says. Her voice is calm. The words are not.

scene_acceptable_losses_polite_roar.narration: Your manticore roars at the map. It is a polite roar, with a please in it, and still every pen rolls off the table. Captain Voss waits for the last pen to stop. Then she redraws one circle so it misses a town.

scene_acceptable_losses_hear_plan.narration: Voss explains, carefully and honestly. Close the roads at the Pinch, the narrow gap ahead. Empty three towns. Stop stones going either way. When she finishes, you can hear the humming.

scene_acceptable_losses_not_a_number.narration: "A town is not a number," you say. Voss looks at the map a long time. "No. It's three numbers. Houses, people, bells." Then, very quietly: "I know." She draws one circle a little smaller.

scene_whole_truth_window.narration: "One cup of tea before the record," says Pellam. From the window you see three kinds of light: Hessa's moving lantern, the glittering camps, and the bell towers of the dragonling towns. Which do you watch?

scene_whole_truth_window_soup.narration: Hessa's lantern is the only light that moves. She carries soup to the tents nobody else visits. It looks very kind. It looks very certain, too. Pellam writes nothing, and keeps watching.

scene_whole_truth_window_camps.narration: The camps glitter like a dropped necklace. Every tent has a stone in it. When you hold very still, you can hear them: thousands of stones, humming the same old note, a long way from home.

scene_whole_truth_window_bells.narration: One by one, the dragonling towns ring the ordinary night bell, passed from town to town like a lantern down a line. Then they all go quiet. Captain Voss counts every ring under her breath, and looks more relieved at each one.

scene_whole_truth_window_wolf.narration: Down on the dark road, one small glow sits apart from its pack, round with sausage. It is the wolf from the road. Cinder wolves do not wave. This one thumps its tail twice, which is close.

scene_whole_truth_window_look_up.narration: You look up, the way the whole citadel does. Over Mount Red Sky, the sky is a deep, wrong red. The mountain puffs out ash, slow, like somebody breathing in their sleep. "Somebody writes that down every night," says Pellam softly. "Tonight it's me."

scene_whole_truth_window_ring.narration: Ding, ding-ding, ding, softly, into the dark. Far below, a very small bell answers: ding, dong, clatter. The smallest dragonling is still up, practicing. Captain Voss turns away so nobody sees her smile.

scene_ledger.narration: Pellam opens a fresh page. "What have you been doing, all this way?" Tell it in your own words, or point to something you did.

variants.text: The page beside your names stays short. Pellam writes down a hum, and little else.
Beside your names Pellam lists the great stones you carry: {facets} so far, each logged twice.
Pellam needs a second page for the great stones you carry: {facets}, each logged twice.
Pellam records your first reason: treasure. He has heard that one before.
Your first reason was finding out what happened. "Today you did," says Pellam.
You wanted your names known. Pellam writes them extra big.
You came to keep people safe. Pellam nods before writing it.
You came for a fresh start. Pellam finds a clean page.
You came to prove you could. "Here you are," says Pellam.
Under WHICH ROAD he writes: the river roads, past the prides and the broken bridge.
Under WHICH ROAD he writes: the forest roads, through MossHome and the high paths.
Under WHICH ROAD he writes: the rush roads, past the boundary stones.

scene_reading_restore.narration: Pellam reads it all back and taps the page. "Helping. Fixing. Putting things back where they belong. That adds up to one word, and the word is return." Captain Voss raises one eyebrow, which for her is practically a parade.

scene_reading_hoard.narration: Pellam reads it back, and the stone on the table hums along. "Pockets," he says. "A great many pockets. That adds up to a collection." Nobody says he is wrong. A moth lands on your bag, thinks about it, and leaves.

scene_reading_leash.narration: Pellam reads it back slowly. "Questions about what the power could do. Who holds it. What it's for." He writes one word and underlines it twice: leash. Far below, Hessa's soup tent is still serving.

scene_who_to_tell.narration: "Who should stand with you now?" asks Voss. "The wardens, the grandmothers' towns, or nobody else yet?" If you made a promise on the road, you can keep it, or choose again after what you learned. She waits.

choices.label: Keep our word to the wardens

scene_kept_close_room.narration: "Nobody else," says Captain Voss. "Then you had better be right, and you had better be quick." Pellam writes nothing at all, which he says later is the best entry a ledger can have.

scene_told_gatherers_room.narration: "Grandmothers," sighs Captain Voss, like somebody who has argued with grandmothers before. "Very well. They are at least thorough." Pellam writes BELLS and underlines it. Far below, right on cue, one rings.

scene_told_wardens_room.narration: Captain Voss nods once, which is as much as she ever nods. "Then you'll want the plan properly." Pellam opens a fresh ledger with WARDENS AND PARTY on the spine. He has clearly had it ready for some time.

scene_what_for.narration: "And you? What is it all for?" asks Voss. Return the stones, finish the collection, or learn to hold the power. At the mountain you will face this question again. Or say nothing for now, and leave on the return road.

scene_declared_leash.narration: "Hold it. The leash." Voss and Pellam look at each other. "Our plan, in fewer words," she says. Below the window, the soup-tent choir hums.

scene_record_leash.narration: "Leash," Pellam says, and underlines it twice. "Holding is harder than asking. You have to know you are choosing it." Captain Voss closes the book.

variants.text: First entry: the city's warm stone, sold the same day.
First entry: the city's warm stone, kept.
Then the harvest sprites, still your friends. He draws a tiny star.
Then the stone you took from the harvest sprites. He reads that one twice.
Then the wounded glade, green again because of you.
Then the wounded glade, and the stone you took out of its heart.
"Helping. Fixing. Putting things back," Pellam reads. "That is not the same as holding a leash," says Voss.
"Pockets. A great many pockets," Pellam reads. "That is not the same as holding a leash," says Voss.
"Questions about the power, and who holds it," Pellam reads. "You have been asking about the leash all the way up," says Voss.

scene_declared_hoard.narration: "Finish the collection." Voss considers it. "Then I will write you down as weather." Pellam writes WEATHER, then adds a question mark. The ink takes a long time to dry.

scene_record_hoard.narration: "Collection," Pellam says, and writes COLLECT in his neatest hand, with a small question mark. Captain Voss watches the ink dry. "You will have to live up to that word," she says.

variants.text: First entry: the city's warm stone, sold the same day.
First entry: the city's warm stone, kept.
Then the harvest sprites, still your friends. He draws a tiny star.
Then the stone you took from the harvest sprites. He reads that one twice.
Then the wounded glade, green again because of you.
Then the wounded glade, and the stone you took out of its heart.
"Helping. Fixing. Putting things back," he reads. "That is a different word from the one you just said."
"Pockets. A great many pockets," he reads. "Nobody can say you didn't warn us."
"Questions about the power, and who holds it," he reads. "That is a different word from the one you just said."

scene_declared_restore.narration: "Put it back. Every stone." The table answers with one clear note. Voss unfolds her arms. "Then we need the stones coming north tomorrow. Rest first."

scene_record_restore.narration: "Put it back," Pellam says, and writes RETURN beside your names. He leaves a little space after it, in case the road teaches you something else. Captain Voss nods.

variants.text: First entry: the city's warm stone, sold the same day.
First entry: the city's warm stone, kept.
Then the harvest sprites, still your friends. He draws a tiny star.
Then the stone you took from the harvest sprites. He reads that one twice.
Then the wounded glade, green again because of you.
Then the wounded glade, and the stone you took out of its heart.
"Helping. Fixing. Putting things back," Pellam reads. "The pages and the promise agree."
"Pockets. A great many pockets," Pellam reads. "And now you say put it back. People do turn around," says Voss.
"Questions about the power, and who holds it," Pellam reads. "And now you say put it back. People do turn around," says Voss.

scene_undeclared.narration: Pellam writes RETURN, with a question mark. "A starting road, then," says Voss. "You can carry a question as well as a plan." She leaves your earlier promises in the record.

rest_end_ashfall.narration: The wardens give you bunks in a room where every window faces up. Far below, the mountain turns over in its sleep. You know what the stones are now, and what you want. Tomorrow, everything you passed on the road comes up the mountain to meet you.

variants.text: The traveling call you learned brought a lantern to the gate.
Your record includes the people who helped compare the evidence.

scene_shut_out.narration: You spend the night outside the gate. At midnight a little hatch opens. A warden clerk called Pellam passes out the old watch-logs by lantern and reads you the oldest line. The gemstones are pieces of a seal. The seal holds a titan asleep under Mount Red Sky. And the rush is taking it apart, one pocket at a time. "What is it all for?" he whispers. Take time to hear one another before answering.

scene_shut_out_refuse.narration: "The return road, for now," Pellam whispers after your silence. "The question stays open." He passes a blanket through the hatch, then another.

scene_shut_out_leash.narration: "Hold it," you whisper. "The leash." The pen stops. "That's my captain's word," Pellam whispers, puzzled. He passes out a blanket and a tiny book with CAGE on the spine, and asks for it back in the morning.

scene_shut_out_hoard.narration: "Finish the collection," you whisper. There is a pause behind the hatch. "Noted," Pellam whispers at last. After another pause, a blanket comes through anyway.

scene_shut_out_restore.narration: "Put it back," you whisper through the hatch. Pellam's pen scratches. "Good," he whispers back, which is not a thing clerks say. A blanket follows the lantern.

rest_end_shut_out.narration: You sleep against the cold citadel wall, like the embermoths. The crabs, the sunset and the gate all beat you today. But the whole truth is in your heads now, and Pellam's lantern burns on the wall all night.

variants.text: The traveling call you learned brought a lantern to the gate.
Your record includes the people who helped compare the evidence.

scene_crab_long_way.narration: You back everybody off the warm ground, Dunmore last and grumbling, and take the goat track around the ridge. It is a goat's idea of a road. By the time it reaches the citadel side, the morning is gone.

scene_truth_table_charm.narration: You set Mother Thrum's tuned charm on the table. It rings, and the stone on the table rings back. Every warden stops writing at once. Captain Voss waits for the note to fade. It takes a long time.

interaction_moth_trail.narration: One moth glows brighter, then hides between three flat rocks. Follow where it ends up. The soup prospector watches too, with his bowl well out of range.

interaction.cue: Watch the glowing moth hide, then pick the rock it ends up under.

onSuccess.narration: Right rock! The moth pops out glowing like a tiny stove and flutters down toward the caravan road.

onFailure.narration: Wrong rock. The moth peeks out from the right one, giggles, if moths can giggle, and zips down toward the caravan road.

interaction_wagons.narration: A wagon wheel is stuck in a rut, blocking the road again. Push while someone steers. "I'll pull!" says the centaur drover. Everybody behind you offers excellent advice.

interaction.cue: Friends push the wagon while someone steers.

onSuccess.narration: The wheel pops out like a cork. Forty drovers say it was their idea. The centaur drover gives you three coins. "Toll refund. Do not ask which toll."

onFailure.narration: The wagon rolls back, then forward, then sideways. In the end a faun drover hitches a goat to it, and it pops free. Everybody pretends that was the plan.

onAssisted.narration: The drovers lean in beside you, and the wagon rocks free. The centaur drover gives you three coins. "Toll refund."

interaction_soup_pots.narration: You help Hessa's helpers carry the hot supper pots down the line. At the last tent, a tired prospector cups a bowl and stops shivering. Hessa wraps a supper for your pack. "For the road," she says.

scene_morning_bells_bought.narration: The bench stall belongs to a dragonling baker with flour on both ears. Two coins buys a warm honeycake as big as a fist. "Eat it on the way up," says the baker. "The ridge is steep."

scene_crawlers_hall.narration: Bone crawlers clack up the cellar stairs, chasing the hum of the logged stones. They are beetles the size of bread loaves, fond of chewing table legs. "Please get them downstairs before they find the old logs!" says Pellam. His pen keeps moving.

encounter_crawlers.narration: The bone crawlers clack along the gallery after the hum. Herd them back to the cellar stairs before they reach the old logs.

scene_crawlers_home.narration: The last crawler clacks downstairs. Pellam shuts the door and writes CRAWLERS: HOME. Then he gives you a tin whistle stamped with a tiny tower. "Warden's issue. For loud moments. Log it if you use it." He straightens his collar. "Now, the tags."

scene_crawlers_rescued.narration: A line of wardens marches in with brooms and sweeps the crawlers downstairs like autumn leaves. Nobody is hurt. Someone hands you hot tea. Pellam writes your names in the margin anyway. "Now, the tags," he says.

interaction_tags.narration: Every humming thing in the citadel gets a picture tag. "Watch them go by," says Pellam, "then put them back in order. The captain likes order."

interaction.cue: Watch the tags light up, then tap them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Moon, flame, leaf, flame. Pellam gives a tiny, rare smile. "The captain will be thrilled," he says. "She will not show it."

onFailure.narration: You swap two tags. Pellam sighs and fixes them with his pen. "Order matters," he says kindly. "It will do. The captain is waiting."

interaction_tea.narration: Pellam pours the tea. Captain Voss takes the smallest cup and drinks without a word. For a while the only question is Pellam's: "More tea, anyone?" Then he turns to a fresh page.

interaction_doorstep.narration: Stand with the grandmother while one hero guides Dunmore's pick away from her step. On your own, lean on the doorpost. Her cookie tin is safe behind the door.

interaction.cue: Hold the doorstep clear while the pick is guided aside.

onSuccess.narration: You plant your feet beside the grandmother. Nobody can dig up a doorstep with people on it. Dunmore goes pinker than ever. "Sorry," he mumbles, and pulls up his flag. She gives him a cookie.

onFailure.narration: Dunmore's pick nudges your boots off the step. Then the grandmother rings her bell right by his ear, and he stomps off up the slope.

onAssisted.narration: The grandmother braces the doorframe beside you. Together you hold the step. Dunmore apologizes, and remembers your voices.

interaction_morning_ring.narration: Grandmother Tull teaches the traveling call: one ring, two quick rings, one ring. Watch, then echo it. "The ridge watch knows this one," she says. "Ring it at the gate and they'll notice you."

interaction.cue: Watch the traveling call, then ring it in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Ding, ding-ding, ding. The smallest dragonling gives you a solemn nod. Grandmother Tull presses a warm honeycake into your hands for the climb.

onFailure.narration: Ding, dong, clatter. In bell code that means goats, but sideways. One little dragonling laughs so hard it falls off the bench. Tull points you up the ridge.

onAssisted.narration: Tull rings beside you while you echo the call. You learn it, and earn a honeycake for the climb.

scene_gate_recovery.narration: Back at the bottom of the ridge, you can see the citadel gate starting to close. Run the switchbacks, or ring the traveling call for the ridge watch if you learned it. A goat waits at the shortest bend.

interaction_gate_call.narration: Ring the traveling call from the morning: one, two quick, one. Tap the rhythm on the gate bell. Far up the wall, a warden lifts a lantern to listen.

interaction.cue: Echo the traveling call for the ridge watch.

onSuccess.narration: The watch answers and holds the gate while you climb. You arrive late, but you arrive.

onFailure.narration: The watch cannot make out the call before the gate shuts. A lantern stays lit by the hatch.

onAssisted.narration: The watch echoes the first ring. You finish together, and the warden holds the gate.

interaction_truth_timeline.narration: Pellam lays out an old watch-log, the eruption report, and this season's road news. Put them in order, oldest first, and see what was already happening. One page has a four-hundred-year-old tea ring.

interaction.cue: Share the dated evidence and place oldest to newest.
clues: The watch-log records the same humming note before the great eruption.
The great eruption happened before the road accounts you brought.
This season's road accounts are the newest records.

onSuccess.narration: The dates line up. Voss opens the oldest explanation beside them.

onFailure.narration: Pellam fixes the order beside you. Voss brings the oldest explanation to the table.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam checks each date with you. Then Voss opens the oldest explanation.

interaction_watch_logs.narration: The wardens read their logs aloud. Stop them to ask questions, or add something from your road. Pellam finds the oldest page under a newer one labeled READ THIS FIRST. He is offended for both pages.

interaction_purpose_council.narration: Before you choose a road, everyone gets a turn. Say what you want to protect, what you still need to know, or what you are willing to try. Pellam puts down his pen. "For once," he says, "the ledger can wait."

choices.label: Say what I want to protect
Ask what our plan might cost
Say what I am willing to try

interaction_watch_logs_response_date.narration: Pellam reads the old date aloud. The wardens answer your questions. Voss turns to the oldest explanation.

interaction_watch_logs_response_road.narration: Voss sets your road beside the watch records. The wardens answer your questions. Voss turns to the oldest explanation.

interaction_watch_logs_response_question.narration: Pellam sorts the known facts from the open questions. Voss turns to the oldest explanation.

interaction_purpose_council_response_pro.narration: The table listens to what you want to keep safe. Now choose your next road together.

interaction_purpose_council_response_ask.narration: Voss hears your question and gives everyone time to talk it over. Now choose your next road together.

interaction_purpose_council_response_try.narration: Pellam listens, and writes nothing beside your name. Now choose your next road together.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, a little spooky, the big reveal told plainly and kindly; grown-ups being rigid or certain, never cruel
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.hessa: Hessa Wren, Deep Hollow Cult cell contact running a soup tent; warm, generous, remembers every name, completely certain the seal is a cage on the cure
npcVoices.captain: Captain Orla Voss of the Skywardens; rigid, honest, never wastes a word, says 'acceptable losses' as calmly as ordering breakfast
npcVoices.pellam: Pellam, warden clerk; writes everything down twice, proud that the best log entry is 'nothing', secretly kind
npcVoices.grandmother_tull: Grandmother Tull, dragonling bell-keeper; brisk, cozy, says 'nothing to worry about' one time too many
npcVoices.dunmore: Dunmore, a prospector with a pick and no sense; embarrassed easily, means well
npcVoices.claim_pair: two prospectors sharing one humming boulder; stubborn, then sheepish, and hungry the whole time

interaction_soup_pots.narration: Pass Hessa's heavy soup pot along to the tents with no supper. "Many hands. No hurry." Every helper takes a handle. One prospector measures his bowl against the pot, hopefully.

interaction.cue: Catch the pot, then pass it on.

onSuccess.narration: The pot goes from hand to hand to hand, all the way to the edge of the camp, and not a drop is lost. A tired prospector takes a bowl in both hands and closes his eyes. Hessa wraps a supper in a cloth and tucks it into your pack. "For the road," she says. It is a very nice supper.

onFailure.narration: The pot wobbles, and half the soup goes into a prospector's boots. He says it is the warmest his feet have been all week. Hessa laughs, and the pots go on.

onAssisted.narration: Hessa's helpers fill the gaps in the line, and the pot goes from hand to hand to the edge of the camp without a drop lost. Hessa wraps a supper in a cloth and tucks it into your pack. "For the road," she says.

interaction_tea.narration: Back at the table, Pellam keeps his word about the tea. The kettle is the size of a bucket, and the cups are the size of thimbles. "Everybody helps with tea," he says. "It is in the regulations. Page nine."

interaction.cue: Make the tea: pour it, stir it and share the shortbread.

options.label: Pour the tea
options.reaction: A thin gold stream fills a thimble cup without a drop spilled.

options.label: Stir it slowly
options.reaction: The tea swirls round and round, and a warden leans in to watch.

options.label: Pass the shortbread
options.reaction: Pellam takes one piece and logs it. Then he takes another piece and does not log it.

stages: Everybody has a cup and a piece of shortbread.

onSuccess.narration: The tea is only slightly too hot. Captain Voss drinks hers in one go without a word, and puts the cup down very gently, which from her is a compliment. Pellam turns to a fresh page.

onFailure.narration: The tea is only slightly too hot. Captain Voss drinks hers in one go without a word, and puts the cup down very gently, which from her is a compliment. Pellam turns to a fresh page.

interaction_watch_logs.narration: Let the wardens read the logs, and stop them to ask questions. Each hero chooses something to check or offers a road observation. Pellam finds the oldest page under a newer page labeled READ THIS FIRST. He is offended on behalf of both pages.

interaction.cue: Each hero checks a record or adds an observation.

options.label: Ask how old the matching note is
options.reaction: Pellam points to the old date and reads it aloud.

options.label: Describe a change on our road
options.reaction: Voss sets your observation beside the watch records.

options.label: Ask what the records cannot explain
options.reaction: Pellam separates the recorded facts from the questions still open.

onSuccess.narration: The wardens answer your questions and compare the dated records. Voss turns to their oldest explanation.

onFailure.narration: Pellam finishes reading the dates with you. Voss turns to the oldest explanation.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam helps you check the records one question at a time. Voss turns to the oldest explanation.

interaction_purpose_council.narration: Before choosing a road, hear every hero. Say what you hope to protect, what you still need to know, or what you are willing to try. You may ask for help finding words. Pellam puts his pen down. For once, the ledger can wait.

interaction.cue: Each hero shares a hope, a question or a concern before the vote.

options.label: Say what I want to protect
options.reaction: The table listens to what you hope to keep safe.

options.label: Ask what our plan might cost
options.reaction: Voss hears your question and leaves time for everyone to discuss it.

options.label: Say what I am willing to try
options.reaction: Pellam listens without putting a choice beside your name.

onSuccess.narration: Everyone has had a turn. Now choose the party's next road together.

onFailure.narration: The table leaves room for your questions, then waits for the party's decision.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam asks gentle questions while you find the words. Everyone gets a turn before the party decides.
